title: Alberta cops cleared in shootings
article: Two Calgary city cops and a pair of Mounties have been cleared of any wrongdoing in separate officer- involved shootings, one of them deadly.

The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) has concluded its investigation into the Jan. 10 fatal shooting of armed robbery suspect Steven Boucher in Canmore and found Mounties were justified when they shot him three times, fatally wounding him.
After being stopped in the town, Boucher, who was suspected of a robbery half an hour prior, stepped out of this car, refused verbal commands by police, and pointed a gun at an officer.
The weapon was later determined to be a replica air soft pistol intended to resemble a 45-calibre Smith and Wesson handgun.
ASIRT executive director Clifton Purvis said as soon as the gun was shown, an officer tried taking cover in his car, at which point 11 shots were fired by two RCMP members.
The investigation, which included eyewitness accounts from civilans and an off-duty police officer, revealed RCMP were acting lawfully when they opened fire.
"This replica firearm was virtually identical to the real firearm and I have determined both police officers would not have been able to identify it as a replica," he said.

Purvis could not conclude, however, whether Boucher had a suicidal wish to be killed by police. "It's not our place to speculate what would have caused his behaviour. We were unable to uncover anything definitive that would have explained why he did what he did," he said, calling the incident a "tragedy for everybody."

ASIRT has also found two Calgary cops were in the right to shoot a 22-year-old man Feb. 8, 2010, during a traffic stop in McKenzie Lake. One officer was struck by the suspect's car, at which time the man was shot twice, once in the face and once in his hand.
Purvis refused to divulge more details about the case, including whether both officers fired their guns, because the victim is the subject of an ongoing police investigation.
